keyword: PCGS NGC certified silver coins guide
angle: A buyer's guide to understanding how PCGS and NGC certification grades—especially MS69, MS70, and PF70—drive significant premiums over raw silver bullion, and how to decide whether paying those premiums makes sense for your collection or investment strategy.

stats.claim: 28 of the top 30 highest-priced coins sold at auction in 2024 were certified by PCGS, representing 93% of the top auction hammer results by lot count.
A 2026 American Silver Eagle graded MS70 retails for approximately $210, compared to roughly $82 for a standard uncertified bullion coin—a premium of approximately 156% over raw bullion.
PCGS-graded coins typically command 5–15% higher prices than identical NGC-graded coins in most U.S. coin series, reflecting PCGS's stronger brand equity in the domestic classic coin market.
NGC has graded 15,603,470 American Silver Eagles total, of which 5,234,192 (approximately 34%) received a perfect grade of MS70.
The global coin collection market was valued at $11.87 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $23.87 billion by 2032, a 10.5% CAGR driven in part by demand for professionally graded assets.
PCGS has certified over 60.5 million coins, banknotes, medals, and tokens with a combined declared value exceeding $58.3 billion.
